explanation: The thumbs-up is understood across Indonesia as a positive signal for 'good' or 'okay,' and no source found describes it as offensive in Java, Sumatra, or anywhere else in the country. It is a separate gesture from the well-documented Indonesian custom of pointing with the thumb (instead of the index finger) as a politeness norm. Both uses of the thumb are fine for visitors.
local_tip: Use a thumbs-up freely for approval, and if you need to indicate a person or direction, point with your thumb rather than your index finger, as many Indonesians do.

also_check.note: Thumbs-up is considered an obscene insult, similar to the middle finger in the West.
Thumbs-up reads as a friendly 'good' or 'okay' signal.
Older or more traditional Greeks may still see it as rude, though it's increasingly read as positive among younger people.

sources.title: A Thumb Points the Way in Java
